#Graph 1: mean curves
summary_dat <- dat %>%
  group_by(condition, delay_ms) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_rating = mean(probability_rating, na.rm = TRUE),
    se = sd(probability_rating, na.rm = TRUE) /
      sqrt(sum(!is.na(probability_rating))),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

write.csv(
  summary_dat,
  "~/Desktop/summary_dat.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
ggplot(
  summary_dat,
  aes(
    x = delay_ms,
    y = mean_rating,
    color = condition,
    group = condition
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = mean_rating - se,
      ymax = mean_rating + se
    ),
    width = 15
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    x = "Temporal delay (ms)",
    y = "Mean causal judgment",
    color = "Condition"
  )

)

## Warning: Removed 4 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_line()`).
## Warning: Removed 4 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_point()`).

model_dat <- dat %>%
  select(participant, condition, block, direction, delay_ms, probability_rating, trial) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(participant),
    !is.na(condition),
    !is.na(block),
    !is.na(delay_ms),
    !is.na(probability_rating)
  ) %>%
  droplevels()

model_dat$block <- factor(model_dat$block)
model_dat$participant <- factor(model_dat$participant)
model_dat$condition <- factor(model_dat$condition)
model_dat$delay_ms <- as.numeric(model_dat$delay_ms)
model_dat$probability_rating <- as.numeric(model_dat$probability_rating)
colnames(model_dat)
## [1] "participant"        "condition"          "block"             
## [4] "direction"          "delay_ms"           "probability_rating"
## [7] "trial"
levels(model_dat$condition)
## [1] "intact"    "scrambled"
levels(model_dat$participant)
##  [1] "s003" "s005" "s006" "s007" "s008" "s009" "s010" "s011" "s012" "s013"
## [11] "s014" "s015" "s018" "s020" "s021" "s022" "s023" "s024" "s025" "s026"
## [21] "s027" "s028" "s029" "s030" "s031" "s032"
model_dat$trial_id <- interaction(
  model_dat$participant,
  model_dat$condition,
  model_dat$delay_ms,
  drop = TRUE
)
# ============================================================
# 3. BLOCK EFFECT
# ============================================================

block_summary <- model_dat %>%
  group_by(block, condition) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_rating = mean(probability_rating),
    se = sd(probability_rating) / sqrt(n()),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

block_summary
## # A tibble: 8 × 5
##   block condition mean_rating    se     n
##   <fct> <fct>           <dbl> <dbl> <int>
## 1 1     intact           71.6  1.92   221
## 2 1     scrambled        53.5  2.25   221
## 3 2     intact           55.5  1.98   221
## 4 2     scrambled        68.3  1.96   221
## 5 3     intact           71.2  1.75   221
## 6 3     scrambled        51.7  2.21   221
## 7 4     intact           59.3  1.97   221
## 8 4     scrambled        64.0  2.03   221
ggplot(
  block_summary,
  aes(
    x = block,
    y = mean_rating,
    group = condition,
    color = condition
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = mean_rating - 1.96 * se,
      ymax = mean_rating + 1.96 * se
    ),
    width = 0.1
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    labels = paste("Block", levels(model_dat$block))
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 100),
    breaks = seq(0, 100, 20)
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    x = "Block",
    y = "Causal judgment",
    color = "Condition",
    title = "Causal judgments across 4 blocks"
  )

#two random-effect levels: participant captures overall individual differences, while trial_id captures the correlation among the repeated observations of the same participant–condition–delay combination.

gamm_repeat <- gam(
  probability_rating ~
    condition +
    s(delay_ms, by = condition, k = 8) +
    s(participant, bs = "re") +
    s(trial_id, bs = "re"),
  data = model_dat,
  method = "REML"
)

#If the main purpose is just to account for the fact that the same participant sees the same unique stimulus X times, we can model that dependence using trial_id without necessarily including a repeat-number fixed effect (which asks whether participants systematically change their judgments from the first to the Xth presentation).
#Here we ask: Does the condition-specific nonlinear temporal relationship hold after accounting for differences between participants [1] and repeated observations of the same participant × condition × delay stimulus [2]?
gam.check(gamm_repeat)

## 
## Method: REML   Optimizer: outer newton
## full convergence after 7 iterations.
## Gradient range [-2.299585e-05,1.197648e-05]
## (score 7974.32 & scale 287.7404).
## Hessian positive definite, eigenvalue range [1.746668,961.9208].
## Model rank =  926 / 926 
## 
## Basis dimension (k) checking results. Low p-value (k-index<1) may
## indicate that k is too low, especially if edf is close to k'.
## 
##                                    k'    edf k-index p-value    
## s(delay_ms):conditionintact      7.00   6.13    0.85  <2e-16 ***
## s(delay_ms):conditionscrambled   7.00   6.44    0.85  <2e-16 ***
## s(participant)                  26.00  23.98      NA      NA    
## s(trial_id)                    884.00 508.26      NA      NA    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
model_same <- gam(
  probability_rating ~
    condition +
    block +
    s(delay_ms, k = 8) +
    s(participant, bs = "re") +
    s(trial_id, bs = "re"),
  data = model_dat,
  method = "ML"
)

model_diff <- gam(
  probability_rating ~
    condition +
    block +
    s(delay_ms, by = condition, k = 8) +
    s(participant, bs = "re") +
    s(trial_id, bs = "re"),
  data = model_dat,
  method = "ML"
)

anova(model_same, model_diff, test = "Chisq")

newdat_repeat <- expand.grid(
  delay_ms = seq(
    min(model_dat$delay_ms, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(model_dat$delay_ms, na.rm = TRUE),
    length.out = 300
  ),
  condition = levels(model_dat$condition),
  participant = levels(model_dat$participant)[1],
  trial_id = levels(model_dat$trial_id)[1]
)
#2. Generate population-level predictions
pred_repeat <- predict(
  gamm_repeat,
  newdata = newdat_repeat,
  se.fit = TRUE,
  exclude = c(
    "s(participant)",
    "s(trial_id)"
  )
)
#3. Add confidence intervals
newdat_repeat$fit <- as.numeric(pred_repeat$fit)
newdat_repeat$se <- as.numeric(pred_repeat$se.fit)

newdat_repeat$lower <- newdat_repeat$fit - 1.96 * newdat_repeat$se
newdat_repeat$upper <- newdat_repeat$fit + 1.96 * newdat_repeat$se
summary_dat <- model_dat %>%
  group_by(condition, delay_ms) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_rating = mean(probability_rating, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
#plot
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(
  newdat_repeat,
  aes(
    x = delay_ms,
    y = fit,
    color = condition,
    fill = condition
  )
) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = lower,
      ymax = upper
    ),
    alpha = 0.15,
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = summary_dat,
    aes(
      x = delay_ms,
      y = mean_rating,
      color = condition
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 2.5
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 100, 20)
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    x = "Temporal delay (ms)",
    y = "Causal judgment (0–100)",
    color = "Condition",
    fill = "Condition"
  )
